arxiv-2204-07432.title: ML_LTU at SemEval-2022 Task 4: T5 Towards Identifying Patronizing and Condescending Language
arxiv-2204-07432.creator: Tosin Adewumi, Lama Alkhaled, Hamam Mokayed, Foteini Liwicki, Marcus Liwicki
arxiv-2204-07432.description: Abstract This paper describes the system used by the Machine Learning Group of LTU in subtask 1 of the SemEval-2022 Task 4: Patronizing and Condescending Language (PCL) Detection. Our system consists of finetuning a pretrained Text-to-Text-Transfer Transformer (T5) and innovatively reducing its out-of-class predictions.

arxiv-2211-11330.title: On the Bell experiments; an epistemological approach
arxiv-2211-11330.creator: Inge S. Helland
arxiv-2211-11330.description: Abstract The Nobel prize in physics for 2022 was given for performing Bell experiments with varying degree of sophistication. The interpretation of this experiment is discussed by first recalling Bell’s simple argument behind his inequalities, in particular the CHSH inequality.

arxiv-2212-02816.title: Energy of Decomposition and Entanglement Thermodynamics for T 2 T^{2} -deformation
arxiv-2212-02816.creator: Kuroush Allameh, Amin Faraji Astaneh
arxiv-2212-02816.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kuroush Allameh, Amin Faraji Astaneh. We have presented a set of laws of entanglement thermodynamics for T ​ T ¯ T\bar{T} -deformed CFTs and in general for T 2 T^{2} -deformed field theories. In particular, the first law of this set, states that although we are dealing with a non-trivial deformed theory, the change of the entanglement entropy is simply translated to the change of the bending energy of the entangling surface. We interpret this energy as the energy of decomposition.

arxiv-2406-18601.title: Elementary econometric and strategic analysis of curling matches
arxiv-2406-18601.creator: John Fry, Mark Austin and Silvio Fanzon
arxiv-2406-18601.description: Abstract We develop a Markov model of curling matches, parametrised by the probability of winning an end and the probability distribution of scoring ends. In practical applications, these end-winning probabilities can be estimated econometrically, and are shown to depend on which team holds the hammer, as well as the offensive and defensive strengths of the respective teams.

arxiv-2407-10947.title: Can Textual Semantics Mitigate Sounding Object Segmentation Preference?
arxiv-2407-10947.creator: Yaoting Wang, Peiwen Sun, Yuanchao Li, Honggang Zhang, Di Hu 🖂
arxiv-2407-10947.description: Abstract The Audio-Visual Segmentation (AVS) task aims to segment sounding objects in the visual space using audio cues. However, in this work, it is recognized that previous AVS methods show a heavy reliance on detrimental segmentation preferences related to audible objects, rather than precise audio guidance.

arxiv-2503-01452.title: Reweighting and Analysing Event Generator Systematics by Neural Networks on High-Level Features
arxiv-2503-01452.creator: Amon Furuichi, Sung Hak Lim, Mihoko M. Nojiri
arxiv-2503-01452.description: Abstract The state-of-the-art deep learning (DL) models for jet classification use jet constituent information directly, improving performance tremendously. This draws attention to interpretability, namely, the decision-making process, correlations contributing to the classification, and high-level features (HLFs) representing the difference between signal and background.

arxiv-2509-16313.description: Abstract Synchrotron emission is seen in a vast array of astrophysical transients, such as gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), radio supernovae, neutron star (NS) mergers, tidal disruption events (TDEs), and fast blue optical transients (FBOTs). arxiv-2510-18685.title: Hydrogen redistribution in Zr-base cladding under gradients in temperature and stress Presented in SMiRT-28, August 10-15, 2025, Toronto, Canada .
arxiv-2510-18685.creator: L. O. Jernkvist & A. R. Massih
arxiv-2510-18685.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by L. O. Jernkvist & A. R. Massih. Computational models are used here for simulating diffusion-controlled redistribution of hydrogen that is picked up by zirconium-base nuclear fuel cladding during light water reactor operation. Axial localization of hydrogen, leading to localized precipitation of zirconium hydrides at lower-temperature regions near interpellet gaps, is studied with a bespoke model, while radial diffusion, leading to formation of a densely hydrided rim subjacent to the waterside oxide layer, is studied with a more general model.

arxiv-2510-24512.title: Quality Coefficients for Interferometric Phase Linking
arxiv-2510-24512.creator: Magnus Heimpel *, Irena Hajnsek, Othmar Frey
arxiv-2510-24512.description: Abstract In multi-temporal InSAR, phase linking refers to the estimation of a single-reference interferometric phase history from the information contained in the coherence matrix of a distributed scatterer. Since the phase information in the coherence matrix is typically inconsistent, the extent to which the estimated phase history captures it must be assessed to exclude unreliable pixels from further processing.

pmc-10546724.description: BackgroundThe genetic underpinnings of late-onset Alzheimer’s disease (LOAD) are yet to be fully elucidated. pmc-13599187.title: A lesion-derived brain network of somatic symptoms for transdiagnostic individual application
pmc-13599187.creator: Yue Yu, Wenqiang Xu, Yang Ji, Li Qi, Yue Wu, Yuanyuan Guo, Qiang Hua, Lihong Wang, Rui Qian, Tongjian Bai, Qianqian Li, Feng Geng, Yuhui Wan, Kai Wang, Gong-Jun Ji, Yanghua Tian
pmc-13599187.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSomatic symptoms is an umbrella term that describes distressing somatic complaints occurring across a wide spectrum of diseases. However, their underlying neural mechanisms remain poorly understood. Elucidating their mechanisms could therefore benefit patients with diverse conditions.MethodsUsing a recently validated lesion network mapping method and a large-scale healthy connectome database (n = 652, recruited in Anhui Province, China), we identified a somatic network from brain lesions causing somatic symptoms.

pmc-13695582.title: ADBrainNet: a deep neural network for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention Deficit and Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) classification using resting-state fMRI images based on explainable artificial intelligence
pmc-13695582.creator: Xinyao Yi, Jian Huang, Babatunde Akinwunmi, Wai-kit Ming
pmc-13695582.description: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention Deficit and Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) are two psychiatric disorders frequently encountered in children. ADHD is further categorized into three subtypes. The diagnostic processes for these conditions are complex and often prone to misclassification. We proposed a lightweight deep neural network, ADBrainNet, to differentiate ASD, ADHD combined, ADHD hyperactive/impulsive, ADHD inattentive and neurotypical individuals.
